title: Pennsylvania's 5th Congressional District election, 2026
jurisdiction: Pennsylvania's 5th Congressional District — Delaware County, southwestern Philadelphia, and parts of Chester and Montgomery counties
description: Pennsylvania's 5th Congressional District covers suburban Delaware County, a portion of South Philadelphia, and slivers of Chester and Montgomery counties. Incumbent Democrat Mary Gay Scanlon, first elected in a 2018 special election and regularly reelected since, is seeking another term against Republican nominee Nick Manganaro, a finance professional and first-time congressional candidate. The district has a strong Democratic lean (Cook PVI D+15) and is rated as Solid/Safe Democratic by nonpartisan analysts, making Scanlon the heavy favorite in a race that reflects broader national partisan dynamics in Pennsylvania's Philadelphia suburbs.
polling_note: No publicly available opinion polls were found for the Pennsylvania 5th Congressional District general election as of June 2026. Nonpartisan race ratings (Cook Political Report: Solid D; Sabato's Crystal Ball: Safe Democratic; Inside Elections: Solid Democratic) indicate a strong Democratic lean with the incumbent as the clear favorite.

candidates.name: Mary Gay Scanlon
candidates.summary: Mary Gay Scanlon is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 5th Congressional District, first elected in 2018 in both a special election and regular election simultaneously. She serves on the House Judiciary Committee and the Committee on Rules, and previously worked as a public interest attorney and pro bono counsel at Ballard Spahr.

forecast.rationale: No district-specific public polling exists as of June 2026, which reduces confidence and prevents direct voter-measurement confirmation. However, structural factors strongly point to a Democratic hold: Pennsylvania's 5th District has a Cook PVI of D+15, covering Democratic-trending Philadelphia suburbs (Delaware County, South Philadelphia). Incumbent Mary Gay Scanlon has held the seat since 2018 and consistently won by large margins. All major nonpartisan race analysts (Cook Political Report: Solid D; Sabato's Crystal Ball: Safe Democratic; Inside Elections: Solid Democratic) rate this as a safe Democratic seat. Republican challenger Nick Manganaro is a first-time congressional candidate, albeit with a strong finance background. Given no polling but overwhelming structural and incumbency advantages, the forecast is safe Democratic with medium confidence.
